chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Al Maghra', from Al Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The most rapid (of supplications) and the quickest (to be answered) is the supplication of a man for his brother in his absence.

key_terms.بِظَهْرِ الْغَيْبِ: In his absence / behind his back

ai.seo_question: What is the most accepted and fastest answered supplication in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the profound spiritual efficacy of intercessory prayer, particularly when offered sincerely during one's absence. Scholars emphasize that 'behind the back' refers to the supplicant's absence from the recipient, highlighting the purity of intent when no audience is present. This act is considered a key mechanism for maintaining communal bonds and accelerating divine response.
